text:
maria (oncall): SLO alert firing: P99 gateway timeouts for hosted-infer in usw2. PD incident P99_TIMEOUT_HOSTED_INFER. Customer CS-8421 reported high latency. Anyone seeing traces?
marcus: Yep, p99 for /v1/generate jumped to ~2.1s around 02:12 UTC, qps steady. No big infra deploys flagged.
ken: Dashboard shows a tail spike correlated with batcher-v2 backlog rising. CPU on batcher nodes is fine, but there's a long socket wait count.
chloe: Logs show a bunch of upstream 502s from prefetch-proxy and intermittent 524/timeout from model-pool. Also several 401->502 patterns which smells like auth handshake retries. Sample: 
```
2026-03-17T02:12:34Z gateway request_id=abc status=502 upstream=model-pool error="handshake timeout"
2026-03-17T02:12:36Z authz token=rotated status=401
```
luis: Tracing coverage low for these requests, lots of missing spans between gateway and prefetch. Might be sampling or SDK instrumentation drop. Quick query I ran: 
```
count by upstream_cluster (logs | filter service=gateway and status>=500 and ts>"2026-03-17T02:00:00Z")
```
shows prefetch-proxy and model-pool as top offenders.
support-ic: Customer CS-8421 sent a repro: repeated small batched requests (batch_size=4) at 30rps, got 5xxs and timeouts. They want ETA.
marcus: Repro locally in staging: run curl loop hitting hosted endpoint with header X-Redwood-Token=valid but rotated quickly, saw same 502 tail. Suspect token refresh race interacting with prefetch handshake.
chloe: Can we confirm if recent auth token rotation rolled out at 02:10? I see config rollout window then. If token rotation + prefetch handshake cause extra auth requests, it could saturate prefetch connection pool and create tail.
ken: I pushed a quick log query: 
```
service:auth OR service:prefetch | stats count() by status,service | sort -count
```
Auth failure rate spikes at same time.
marcus: Mitigation plan: 1) Route traffic away from canary nodes with newest auth change, 2) temporarily increase prefetch upstream connections for usw2 (connection_pool_size +20%), 3) enable fallback model variant for critical customers. Who can flip the canary?
maria (oncall): I'll ack PD and start routing. @ken can you open infra change for connection pool? @chloe can you prepare fallback route? I'll message support to update CS-8421.
ken: Opening change PR and infra ticket now. Will monitor.
chloe: Fallback route ready, will flip to fallback-model-v1 for the affected customer ids. Rolling in 1m.
support-ic: Notifying customer: "we've identified a cause related to recent token rotation and are routing your traffic to a stable variant while we investigate. ETA 30m."
luis: For root cause we need full trace coverage - adding a higher sampling sampler for gateway->prefetch for next 15m. Also capturing tcp stats on prefetch nodes.
marcus: After routing change, p95/p99 dropped back to normal within ~3 minutes. Will keep running the repro to confirm stability.
maria (oncall): PD alert acknowledged. Keeping this thread for postmortem notes. Owners: ken (infra followup), chloe (routing/fallback), marcus (repro + tracing), luis (trace sampling + kvcache checks), maria (oncall coordinator).
pagerduty-bot: Alert P99_TIMEOUT_HOSTED_INFER acknowledged by maria (oncall).
maria (oncall): Next steps: collect logs for 02:08-02:18 window, correlate auth rollout config change, run deeper query for handshake latencies, prepare customer-facing postmortem. I'll create incident ticket INC-2026-0617 and assign owners.
support-ic: Logged CS update and flagged for follow-up when postmortem ready. :thumbsup:
